'''Richard Dolbeer''' is an American biologist. Dolbeer served at the [[U.S. Department of Agriculture]] as an expert on human-wildlife conflicts, especially wildlife and aircraft. He is now a consultant in this area.

== Early life and education ==
Richard Dolbeer was born on August 18, 1945, in [[Jackson, Tennessee]]. In 1967 he received his undergraduate degree in Biology from the [[University of the South]] and then received his master's degree in Zoology from the [[University of Tennessee]] in 1969.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://trace.tennessee.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?referer=https://www.google.com/&httpsredir=1&article=2821&context=utk_gradthes|title=A Study of Population Density, Seasonal Movements and Weight Changes, and Winter Behavior of the Eastern Box Turtle, Terrapene c. carolina L., in Eastern Tennessee |author=Richard Albert Dolbeer|publisher=University of Tennessee, Knoxville|year=1969}}</ref> He earned his PhD in Wildlife Biology from [[Colorado State University]].<ref name=Blackwell>{{cite web |url=http://digitalcommons.unl.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1015&context=hwi |title=A Tribute to Richard A. Dolbeer: scientist, innovator, manager, and mentor|date=Fall 2009 |author=Bradley F. Blackwell|page=296|publisher=Human–Wildlife Conflicts}}</ref>

== Research and administrative career ==
Richard Dolbeer is a biologist and [[Ornithology|ornithologist]],<ref name="Sims">{{cite web|url=http://blog.cleveland.com/metro/2009/01/birds_planes_fighting_for_the.html|title=Birds, planes fighting for the skies, Ohio expert says|first1=Damon|last1=Sims|first2=Northeast Ohio Media|last2=Group|website=cleveland.com|date=17 January 2009}}</ref> who has researched population dynamics of pest species, economic assessment of losses, development of practical management techniques for resolving human–wildlife conflicts, and [[integrated pest management]] programs.<ref name=Blackwell /> He is also an expert commentator in the media on the dangers of birds in aviation.<ref name=Bogaisky>{{cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/jeremybogaisky/2019/01/14/blood-in-the-sky-10-years-after-the-miracle-on-the-hudson-bird-strikes-remain-an-unsolved-danger-for-aviation/|title=Blood In The Sky: 10 Years After The Miracle On The Hudson, Bird Strikes Remain An Unsolved Danger For Aviation|first=Jeremy|last=Bogaisky|website=Forbes}}</ref> Following his early ornithological research, according to ''[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]]'' magazine, "After listening to the airport executives’ bird-related angst, Dolbeer decided the time had come for him to shift professional gears: He would henceforth devote himself to preventing midair collisions between birds and planes."<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.wired.com/story/its-a-bird-its-a-plane-the-midair-collisions-menacing-air-travel/|title=It's a Bird! It's a Plane! The Midair Collisions Menacing Air Travel|magazine=Wired|last1=Koerner|first1=Brendan I.}}</ref>

From 1972 to 2008 Dolbeer worked at the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Wildlife Research Center<ref name="Sims" /> in [[Sandusky, Ohio]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/what-is-a-bird-strike/|title=What is a bird strike? How can we keep planes safe from them in the future?|first=Brendan|last=Borrell|website=Scientific American}}</ref> He co-authored the very first course of action for wildlife management at airports with Edward Cleary, entitled ''Wildlife Hazard Management at Airports: A Manual for Airport Personnel'', which is used at airports through North America, Europe, Africa, and South America.<ref name=Krausman>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=2SNnAQAAQBAJ&pg=PA148|title=Wildlife Management and Conservation: Contemporary Principles and Practices|first1=Paul R.|last1=Krausman|first2=James W. Cain|last2=III|date=15 October 2013|publisher=JHU Press|page=148|isbn=9781421409870|via=Google Books}}</ref> He also helped to found the Aviation-Wildlife Research Project of the Department of Agriculture during the 1980s<ref name=Blackwell /> and led it until 2002.<ref name=Krausman />  Between 1997 and 2008 he chaired the [[Bird strike|Bird Strike]] Committee-USA,<ref name=CNN /> a committee coordinating industry and government efforts to reduce collisions between aircraft and birds.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foxnews.com/wires/2009Jan16/0,4670,PlaneinRiverBirdDanger,00.html|title=FOXNews.com – Birds, an aviation hazard, hit 1 in 10,000 flights – Local News – News Articles – National News – US News|website=Foxnews.com}}</ref> While at the Department, he was also the National Coordinator for the Airport Wildlife Hazards Program from 2002 to 2008.<ref name=CNN /> In all his committees, Dolbeer worked with both domestic and foreign government officials to create international techniques for the prevention of bird strikes and the promotion of safety for birds and aircraft.<ref name=Krausman />

Over his time at the Department of Agriculture, he authored about 170 scientific papers and was an associate editor for the ''[[Journal of Wildlife Management]]''.<ref name=Blackwell /> As of 2025, he had over 230 scientific publications.<ref name=Linz /> He is also an elected member of the [[American Ornithological Society]]. In terms of recognition, he is a two-time winner of the Jack H. Berryman Institute Research Award, three-time awardee of the USDA Honor Award, and was given both the Lifetime Achievement Award from Bird Strike Committee U.S.A. and the FAA Excellence in Aviation Research award. He was then the inaugural winner of the Caesar Kleberg Award for Excellence in Applied Wildlife Research from [[The Wildlife Society]] in 2008.<ref name=Blackwell />

== Consultancy ==
Following his position with the Department of Agriculture, Dolbeer became a consultant in the area,<ref name=CNN>{{cite web|url=https://www.cnn.com/2009/TECH/01/15/dolbeer.birdstrikes/index.html#cnnSTCText|title=Biologist: Birds competing for airspace with planes |website=Cnn.com}}</ref> including serving as an advisor to the [[Federal Aviation Administration|FAA]] alongside the USDA.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/06/11/nyregion/at-westchester-airport-bald-eagles-and-their-friends-dare.html|title=At Westchester Airport, Where Bald Eagles (and Their Friends) Dare|first=Christine|last=Negroni|date=10 June 2016|website=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> In 2015 he composed the report Trends in Reporting of Wildlife Strikes for the FAA, which analyzed how many collisions between aircraft and birds in the US. In the report he stated that mandatory reporting of collisions would not be necessary due to the number of voluntary reports issues per year,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ainonline.com/aviation-news/business-aviation/2015-08-10/wildlife-strike-reports-continue-increase|title=Wildlife Strike Reports Continue to Increase|first=Robert P.|last=Mark|website=Aviation International News}}</ref> stating that 42% of bird strikes per year were likely reported.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vox.com/2016/1/19/10789816/airplane-animal-kill|title=Planes killed 13,159 birds in 2014 — and one iguana|first=Sarah|last=Frostenson|date=19 January 2016|website=Vox}}</ref> Dolbeer currently serves as a consultant for the FAA national wildlife strike database, a database he helped establish in the 1990s.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.travelweekly.com/Travel-News/Airline-News/Efforts-mitigate-danger-of-bird-strikes|title=Efforts mitigate danger of aircraft bird strikes: Travel Weekly|website=Travelweekly.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/10/18/opinion/those-hazardous-flying-birds.html|title=Opinion – Those Hazardous Flying Birds|first=Eric|last=Uhlfelder|date=17 October 2013|website=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref>

Through his work, Dolbeer led research projects that developed several methods of deterring birds from being in the landing and take-off paths of airplanes airports and dispersing those that approach the area.<ref name="Sims" /> This has included laser-driven bird dispersal, and working with the [[EPA]] and [[FDA]] to approve foraging repellents and wildlife capture drugs. Dolbeer's techniques led to a “dramatic reduction” in collisions between birds and aircraft at the [[John F. Kennedy International Airport]]<ref name=Krausman /> as well as several others. He also co-authored reports on the increase of bird strikes in US airspace,<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://content.time.com/time/printout/0,8816,1872175,00.html|title=The US Airways Crash: A Growing Bird Hazard -- Printout -- TIME|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]}}</ref> which he attributed to several factors, including the advent of quieter aircraft,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.spiegel.de/international/world/miracle-on-the-hudson-how-airlines-try-to-avert-growing-bird-strike-risk-a-602092.html|title='Miracle on the Hudson': How Airlines Try to Avert Growing Bird Strike Risk|newspaper=Der Spiegel|date=19 January 2009|publisher=Spiegel Online}}</ref> as well as increases in populations of large-bird species near airports.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.americanscientist.org/article/keeping-birds-out-of-jet-engines|title=Keeping Birds Out of Jet Engines|date=7 December 2018|website=American Scientist}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Dolbeer was an elected official with the Board of Education in [[Huron, Ohio]] from 1981–1989.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.huronhs.com/Downloads/December%202018%20Newsletter2.pdf|title=HHSAA Newsletter : Vol. XVI, No. 2|date=December 2018|website=Huronhs.com|accessdate=26 February 2019}}</ref> In addition to his consultancy work, he also manages a 60-acre wildlife sanctuary, [https://www.bluebirdhaven.org Bluebird Haven], near his home. He was married to his wife Saundra for fifty years,<ref name=Linz>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Gns2DwAAQBAJ&pg=PT15|title=Ecology and Management of Blackbirds (Icteridae) in North America|first1=George M.|last1=Linz|first2=Michael L.|last2=Avery|first3=Richard A.|last3=Dolbeer|date=19 September 2017|publisher=CRC Press|isbn=9781351643559|via=Google Books}}</ref> until her death in 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://obits.cleveland.com/obituaries/cleveland/obituary.aspx?n=saundra-anne-dolbeer&pid=185937692&fhid=13125 |title=SAUNDRA ANNE DOLBEER 1945–2017 |publisher=The Cleveland Plain Dealer |date=July 2, 2017}}</ref>
